issue.title: Snapshot Restore Bug: Missing Data Display in Kibana due to Failed Repository Connection

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Fixes for quality problems that affect the customer experience

labels.name: Team:Kibana Management
labels.description: Dev Tools, Index Management, Upgrade Assistant, ILM, Ingest Node Pipelines, and more t//

repository.name: kibana
repository.description: Your window into all of your data

issue.body:
**Kibana version:**
8.15.2

**Elasticsearch version:**
8.15.2
**Server OS version:**
Elastic Cloud 

**Describe the bug:**
When having two repositories configured and one is unavailable /app/management/data/snapshot_restore/snapshots only an errormessage is shown but no data.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Configure two snapshot repositories but one wich fails to connect to
2. go to /app/management/data/snapshot_restore/snapshots 

**Expected behavior:**
When having two repositories configured and one is unavailable /app/management/data/snapshot_restore/snapshots should show the data from working repositories + notify with an error message.

body: This behaviour is by design and I'm not really seeing what else we could do in this case given all the other constraints on this API's behaviour. In particular, it offers a sorted and paginated view of the snapshots in all the requested repositories, plus summary statistics, so if even one of them isn't available there's no way we can know what's missing and the results will be (possibly-dangerouly) incorrect.

>This behaviour is by design

I guess I don't understand why a resilient api wasn't designed. 

>so if even one of them isn't available there's no way we can know what's missing and the results will be (possibly-dangerouly) incorrect

Doesn't strike me as different from unavailable shards. Return the results and report what was missing.

> I guess I don't understand why a resilient api wasn't designed.

As mentioned above: pagination. I'm guessing this UI isn't really doing `GET /_snapshot/*/*` since this would attempt to retrieve all snapshots, possibly thousands or more. Instead I'd expect it to be using the `?size=` and `?offset=` query params to retrieve the snapshots a page at a time instead. If so, how can we know where the current page even starts if one of the repositories is unavailable? If the unavailability is flaky or temporary then the results will jump around in ways that will suggest that extant snapshots have gone missing.

Moreover the response already indicates what's missing in the message. If it's a repository-level failure and you want to know the contents of the remaining repositories then you can skip the broken repository with e.g. `GET /_snapshot/*,-brokenrepo/...`. However from the screenshots in the linked issue it looks like the UI won't let the user adjust the repository list if this API returns an error:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/996ac4f3-25cc-4b17-8b4d-f0c0f8990800)

That needs fixing, we must expose the repository list so that users can choose to skip the faulty repository.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b83ea8ec-b56c-4ccb-aa82-4348fcd8f143)

Not keen on a UX which requires users to pick which snapshot repo to exclude. Let's put that idea to one side. 

The atomic API behaviour makes sense from one angle, but less so for the practical realities for larger/complex customers with multiple repos who are just trying to manage their estates. Leniency is a preferred experience (along with surfacing relevant errors). e.g. For searching indices with a wildcard, we don't 500 the response if one index is closed or unauthorised. And I think returning partial search results is default.

Considering some options... Perhaps the most lenient option (and imho most usable) would list the snapshots we can and surface an error to say one repo was unauthorized. It sounds like today's APIs would require us to get the results from each repo and then merge and sort results client-side which doesn't sound like a great idea and negates the point of a wildcard. Alternatively we could show a better error perhaps.

Can I see an example of the API response under these circumstances? (the UI shows the elasticsearch errors its given)
What does the Repositories tab look like? Is it showing the problem repo?

To check I understand, you're saying you think it's ok to hide the UI components that would let the user adjust the request parameters and retry in the event of an error? I must be missing something because that seems pretty bad to me. There are possible errors other than just "one repo has incorrect credentials". I imagine we can find a way to handle that one particular case, but the general point about hiding this UI seems more fundamental to me.

Is it possible to create a better error message? Its pretty obtuse.

Yes, we're using pagination.

issue.body:
Today if the get-snapshots API cannot access one of the repositories we
return a fairly low-level message about the problem, perhaps something
like `Could not determine repository generation from root blobs`. This
message is shown verbatim in the Kibana UI so users need something a
little more descriptive. With this commit we wrap the exception in one
that indicates the problem in terms that users are more likely to
understand.

Relates #128208

body: Yep the message is pretty awful today indeed, see https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/128273.

issue.title: Improve get-snapshots behaviour for unreadable repositories

labels.name: :Distributed/Snapshot/Restore
labels.description: Anything directly related to the `_snapshot/*` APIs

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Today if the get-snapshots API cannot access one of the repositories we
return an exception with a fairly low-level message about the problem,
perhaps `Could not determine repository generation from root blobs`.
This message is shown verbatim in the Kibana UI so users need something
a little more descriptive. With this commit we wrap the exception in one
that indicates the problem in terms that users are more likely to
understand.

Moreover, if the user specifies the `?ignore_unavailable` option then we
ignore individual snapshots that are unavailable, treating them as if
they do not exist, but an unavailable repository will still cause the
API to return an exception. With this commit we extend the meaning of
this option to also ignore whole-repository unavailability, treating
unavailable repositories as if they are empty.

Relates #128208
